authors: Robert Schuller | Jens Reinecke | Henry Maurenbrecher | Christian Ott | Alin Albu-Schaeffer | Bastian Deutschmann | Fred Buettner | Jens Heim | Frank Benkert | Stefan Glueck
title: An experimental study of the sensorized strain wave gear RT1-T and its capabilities for torque control in robotic joints
evidence: Independent Lorenz DR-2643 transducers flank the gear (5 Nm drive side and 200 Nm link side, ±0.1% full scale). In a zero-reference manual disturbance test the integrated-feedback mean error averaged 0.65 Nm higher through 0.35 Hz. Above that region both errors increased, which the authors attribute to motor saturation.
rights_and_limitations: CC BY. Controller gains and the manual trajectories differ. The article offers further data from the authors. No export of per-sample limiter state verified.

authors: C. Adrián Pérez-Díaz | Ignacio Muñoz | Daniel Martin-Hernández | Carlos Candelo-Zuluaga | Ivan Torres | Jordi Marsà | Daniel Sanz-Merodio | Miguel López
title: Design and Experimental Characterisation of a Novel Quasi-Direct Drive Actuator for Highly Dynamic Robotic Applications
source_version: Author-uploaded manuscript, March 2024. IEEE ICRA 2024 record https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10611567/
evidence: PULSE115-60 has a separate output torque sensor used for measurement. A 6 Nm test yielded 66.3 Hz mechanical torque bandwidth and 387 Hz electrical current bandwidth.
rights_and_limitations: Public author copy. No redistribution of manuscript or figures. No simultaneous pre/post-limit signals verified.

authors: Iván Jesús Torres Rodríguez | Jordi Marsà Fargas | Carlos Candelo Zuluaga | C. Adrián Pérez Díaz | Luis Daniel Martin Hernández | Daniel Sanz Merodio | Jonay Toledo Carrillo | Miguel López Estévez
title: Toward Reproducible Actuator Characterization: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotics Applications
evidence: Study reports locked-rotor peak steps (0.25 s), 1–1500 Hz excitation, electrical estimates and a separate mechanical transducer. Table 3 gives static bandwidths of 1228.5 Hz (P90) and 1290 Hz (GL80).
rights_and_limitations: CC BY. Record the bandwidth definition for each channel before comparing these numbers with load-side torque. The paper's data statement says no new data were created or analyzed. No raw file identified.

authors: Jörn Malzahn | Navvab Kashiri | Wesley Roozing | Nikos G. Tsagarakis | Darwin G. Caldwell
title: What is the torque bandwidth of this actuator?
source_version: IEEE IROS 2017, author copy. Institutional catalog https://research.utwente.nl/en/publications/what-is-the-torque-bandwidth-of-this-actuator/
evidence: Seven-step procedure accounts for current and voltage envelopes. WALK-MAN leg parameters provide worked examples under locked and inertial loads. The black points in Fig. 8 are simulations.
rights_and_limitations: Public author copy of IEEE paper. Hardware-derived parameters and simulated output provide distinct grades of evidence. No independent shaft-transducer time series verified.

authors: Chan Lee | Sehoon Oh
title: Performance Analysis of Series Elastic Actuator Based on Maximum Torque Transmissibility
source_version: 11-page arXiv:1902.05346 manuscript. IEEE TCST issue 30(1), 392–399, 2022, online 2021
evidence: A 5 Hz peak torque request reaches a current bound. Fixed-load experiments with 1:1 and 36:1 gearing compare motor torque and speed limits. Fig. 7 explains occasional measured speed above the configured limit by drive torque reduction.
rights_and_limitations: arXiv-hosted author manuscript. Joint torque is based on elastic deflection. Independent load-side torque and sample-wise drive-limiter flag were not verified.

authors: José de Gea Fernández | Bingbin Yu | Vinzenz Bargsten | Michael Zipper | Holger Sprengel
title: Design, Modelling and Control of Novel Series-Elastic Actuators for Industrial Robots
evidence: A ±200 Nm external F/T transducer (accuracy class 0.05%) is mounted after the spring. A 9 kg load at 0.8 m is used. Mean absolute deviations for DGMM and linear models were 1.90 and 2.37 Nm (70 Nm chirp), and 0.79 and 1.36 Nm (20 Nm chirp). For the transfer test an offset is estimated over the first 100 samples.
rights_and_limitations: CC BY. The chirp validates torque estimation. The record contains no verified demand/limited-command pair.

authors: Chan Lee | Sehoon Oh
title: Development, Analysis, and Control of Series Elastic Actuator-Driven Robot Leg
source_version: Published journal version, Frontiers in Neurorobotics 13, 17
evidence: A 6 Nm high-frequency chirp trips the drive safety system. Ten 5 Nm sweeps give fitted bandwidths of 32 Hz (free) and 35 Hz (fixed). A separate endpoint-force experiment employs an independent CAS SBA-50L single-axis cell.
rights_and_limitations: CC BY. The joint bandwidth experiment reads elastic deflection. The endpoint load cell belongs to a different experiment.

authors: Jeong Hwan Yoon
title: Experimental Validation of Unlumped Model and Design Implications of its Bandwidth Manifold for Rotary Series Elastic Actuators
evidence: Spring-end F/T sensor sampled at 280 Hz. The fixed-load test uses a 20 Nm chirp from 0.01 to 140 Hz over 160 s plus noise. A 5.8 kg pendulum experiment uses noise. Moving-load phase diverges around 19 Hz, with sensor lag and signal-to-noise ratio discussed.
rights_and_limitations: Author-copyright thesis, publicly accessible. Different excitation by load condition limits comparison. Per-sample clipping was not verified.

authors: Chan Lee | Suhui Kwak | Jihoo Kwak | Sehoon Oh
title: Generalization of Series Elastic Actuator Configurations and Dynamic Behavior Comparison
evidence: Measured frequency responses validate transfer functions for different spring locations. The subsequent controlled comparison of configurations uses MATLAB.
rights_and_limitations: CC BY. Experimental frequency identification and the simulated comparative response have different endpoints. No verified independent torque and clipping combination.

authors: Nicholas Paine | Sehoon Oh | Luis Sentis
title: Design and Control Considerations for High-Performance Series Elastic Actuators
evidence: Fig. 6 distinguishes modeled spring-force and output-force dynamics. Experiments compare desired motor torque times measured speed with measured arm torque times measured velocity. Fig. 15 shows approximately 110 W peak mechanical power.
rights_and_limitations: IEEE author-hosted copy. A spring-force amplification result from the model cannot establish mechanically measured shaft torque or command clipping.

authors: Kyrian Staman | Herman van der Kooij
title: Design and Evaluation of a Torque-Controlled Ankle Exoskeleton Using the Small-Scale Hydrostatic Actuator: miniHydrA
evidence: In the bench friction test, differential pressure-derived force is compared with an independent load cell while the piston moves at constant speed. A connector replaces the hose in this arrangement. Ankle torque follows from force and a geometric moment arm.
rights_and_limitations: CC BY. Raw data on request. This force comparison is on the bench and is distinct from the worn ankle torque estimate.

authors: Sergei V. Sarkisian | Lukas Gabert | Tommaso Lenzi
title: Series-elastic actuator with two degree-of-freedom PID control improves torque control in a powered knee exoskeleton
evidence: An external M3713D six-axis load cell and a linear potentiometer independently measure force and displacement during spring calibration. Linear stiffness was 333 N/mm in compression and 260 N/mm in extension, with R² of 0.996 and 0.989.
rights_and_limitations: Open journal full text. Raw data on request. External cell validates static stiffness in this setup. It does not validate every worn torque sample.

authors: Jack R. Williams | Chance F. Cuddeback | Shanpu Fang | Daniel Colley | Noah Enlow | Payton Cox | Paul Pridham | Zachary F. Lerner
title: OpenExo: An open-source modular exoskeleton to augment human function
source_version: Science Robotics journal PDF read at https://tzechienchu.github.io/mynotes/papers/2025/OpenExo%3A%20An%20open-%C2%ADsource%20modular%20exoskeleton%20to%20augment%20human%20function.pdf
evidence: Inline torque was measured during all benchtop tests. Hip open-loop 6 Nm rise time 3.0 ms, ankle closed-loop 28 Nm 65.0 ms, elbow closed-loop 10 Nm 35.8 ms. The article links its release at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14624972.
rights_and_limitations: Article link and factual measurements only. Excitation amplitudes and physical configurations differ, preventing attribution of the timing differences to feedback alone.

authors: Dean D. Molinaro | Inseung Kang | Aaron J. Young
title: Estimating human joint moments unifies exoskeleton control, reducing user effort
source_version: NSF-hosted Science Robotics 9, eadi8852, 20 March 2024, 12 pages. Dryad README https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi%3A10.5061/dryad.8kprr4xsv
locator: Fig. 1, Methods (study protocol and TCN), Data and materials availability on p. 12
evidence: Hip-moment estimator RMSE was 0.142 Nm/kg across 35 ambulatory conditions. Ground truth uses synchronized motion capture and ground-reaction forces in OpenSim inverse dynamics. The label includes biological plus exoskeleton torque. Paper explicitly points to its 34-participant Dryad deposit.
rights_and_limitations: Public NSF-hosted full text. Dataset README documents missing force-plate windows in overground trials. A joint-moment model label is distinct from independent device output torque.

authors: Qian Mao | Zijian Liao | Shiqiang Liu | Jinfeng Yuan | Rong Zhu
title: An ultralight, tiny, flexible six-axis force/torque sensor enables dexterous fingertip manipulations
locator: Methods (calibration), Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. S6, Data/Code availability ref. 45
evidence: Calibration uses 418 instances, an SH-50 single-axis force gauge (0.01 N resolution) and an angled turntable. Six-axis reference values follow from fixture geometry. The linked author release is https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15553350.
rights_and_limitations: Article CC BY 4.0. The calibration method does not establish a second independent six-axis wrench measurement. Release-specific rights must be checked separately.

authors: Shervin Talebinejad
title: Compliant Running and Step Climbing of the Scout II Platform
evidence: Physical experiment shows controller torque demand, motor-amplifier-derived applied torque, encoder speed and a voltage-model maximum. The nominal 24 V envelope shrinks under load and command exceeds that envelope.
rights_and_limitations: Author copyright. Applied channel is from the amplifier. An independent shaft-torque sensor and per-sample limiter export were not verified.

authors: Xiang-Chen Ku | Yi-Chen Liang | Run-Qing Xue
title: Transformed-domain predefined-time sliding mode control for actuator-constrained trajectory tracking of uncertain robotic manipulators
evidence: Numerical torque clipping at ±80 Nm tests a nominal design analyzed in an unsaturated regime.
rights_and_limitations: Link and bibliographic facts. Simulated bounded commands cannot establish shaft torque, a limiter log, or experimental closed-loop stability.

authors: Patrick M. Wensing | Albert Wang | Sangok Seok | David Otten | Jeffrey Lang | Sangbae Kim
title: Proprioceptive Actuator Design in the MIT Cheetah: Impact Mitigation and High-Bandwidth Physical Interaction for Dynamic Legged Robots
source_version: MIT-hosted author's final manuscript, IEEE T-RO 33(3), 509–522
evidence: Material-test rig compares commanded foot force, winding-current-derived force and external ATI Delta force. Bandwidths calculated from rise time are 400 Hz (driver to current, 0.875 ms) and 103.7 Hz (driver to foot force, 3.38 ms).
rights_and_limitations: MIT-hosted author manuscript. The 103.7 Hz result is a foot-force step estimate. It does not establish a mechanically measured joint shaft sweep.

authors: Simon Kalouche
title: Design for 3D Agility and Virtual Compliance using Proprioceptive Force Control in Dynamic Legged Robots
evidence: A single-axis SRI M2210E reaction-torque load cell measures direct-drive output. At 1.5 Nm the amplitude is maintained to about 70 Hz with nearly 180° phase offset. Small same-sign changes can reach 250 Hz.
rights_and_limitations: Public university-hosted thesis. Excitation amplitudes, signs and phase criteria affect the reported bandwidths. No independent exported limiter fields verified.

authors: Uun Triyas Yuni Kurniawan | Faridah | Sunarno
title: An open-source BLDC motor test bed utilizing ESC telemetry for cost-effective educational laboratories
locator: Fig. 1, §7.3 (torque validation), source file repository table
evidence: ESC telemetry measures electrical variables, while an independent load cell and calibrated lever arm measure brake torque. Reported torque error was below 5%. Steady-state measurements follow manually stabilized brake loads. Dynamic brake steps were tested separately.
rights_and_limitations: Paper CC BY. Article lists hardware under CERN-OHL-S v2. Its permanent archive DOI differs from the one indicated in the GitHub development README, so consult version-specific notes. No demand/limited-command pair verified.

authors: Shijin Chen | Zeyi Liu | Chenyang Li | Dongliang Zou | Xiao He | Donghua Zhou
title: Multi-mode fault diagnosis datasets of three-phase asynchronous motor under variable working conditions
source_version: Data in Brief 65, 112583. Compared with author preprint arXiv:2601.02278v2, 6 February 2026
locator: Specifications Table, Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Table 4, References [4]
evidence: Physical 2.2 kW bench, 282 recordings of 90 s across 12 operating conditions. Eight synchronous raw channels at 12.8 kHz include the S2001 torque sensor (100 mV/Nm, ±0.5% FS) and three measured phase currents. Table 4 describes the nine columns including time.
rights_and_limitations: Published article CC BY. Raw signals are voltages, conversion uses sensitivity. Scheduled load changes and shaft torque do not reveal nested controller demand before and after limiting.

authors: Shijin Chen | Zeyi Liu | Xiao He | Dongliang Zou | Donghua Zhou
title: Multi-mode fault diagnosis datasets of gearbox under variable working conditions
source_version: Data in Brief 54, 110453. Published 18 April 2024. Preprint arXiv:2403.12521v2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12521v2
locator: Specifications Table, Table 1, Fig. 2 and experimental design
evidence: Two triaxial accelerometers monitor the motor and intermediate shaft, a photoelectric sensor records shaft key phase, and a torque sensor measures gearbox input torque. Files represent 60 s runs at 12.8 kHz under varying speeds or loads.
rights_and_limitations: CC BY article. Single-column CSV has no timestamp according to the article. Sensor placement yields gearbox input torque. These data support fault diagnosis, with no verified per-sample unclipped motor command.

authors: Francisco J. Anguita | Rafael Perez-Segui | Carmen DR.Pita-Romero | Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas | Javier Melero-Deza | Pascual Campoy
title: A Comparative Study on Thrust Map Estimation for Multirotor Aerial Vehicles
source_version: IMAV 2025 proceedings pp. 98–105, paper 12. Author spellings in the PDF byline. Proceedings BibTeX lists expanded/variant surnames at https://www.imavs.org/imav2025-proceedings/
evidence: Single- and multiple-rotor stand tests use a TYTO Series 1585 with three force gauges. Step and ramp tests span transient and steady regimes. Flight data refine the resulting map with an estimated correction factor.
rights_and_limitations: Conference-hosted full text and author software repository. Static stand thrust and in-flight estimates are different reference channels. No shaft-torque clipping claim.

authors: Sahand Rezaei-Shoshtari | David Meger | Inna Sharf
title: Learning the Latent Space of Robot Dynamics for Cutting Interaction Inference
locator: Fig. 3, Table I, experimental data and author repo README sections Data and instructions
evidence: 180 real cuts across 12 wood specimens. Jaco2 provides joint proprioception at 10 Hz. Separate specimen-fixture F/T is excluded from the authors' inference model. The repository documents 200 Hz fixture F/T and the need for post-hoc alignment with the ROS streams.
rights_and_limitations: IEEE personal-use manuscript. The linked repository has a BSD-3-Clause LICENSE. Time streams were acquired without synchronization. No implementation of a hardware limiter is inferred.

authors: Aran Mohammad | Moritz Schappler | Tobias Ortmaier
title: Collision Isolation and Identification Using Proprioceptive Sensing for Parallel Robots to Enable Human-Robot Collaboration
evidence: Bench experiments distinguish force-torque sensor measurements projected from known contact locations from the momentum observer available on the robot. Particle filtering with estimated joint torques yielded less than 3 cm localization error and 4 N force error in one real experiment.
rights_and_limitations: IEEE author copy. External joint torque from projection of the contact force is not independent shaft torque. The 2025 author data catalog explicitly assigns the first two tasks to this article.

authors: Aran Mohammad | Moritz Schappler | Tim-Lukas Habich | Tobias Ortmaier
title: Safe Collision and Clamping Reaction for Parallel Robots During Human-Robot Collaboration
evidence: A force-torque sensor measures contact forces solely for evaluation of a planar robot's proprioceptive reactions. The authors report ending contact within 130 ms across tested collision and clamping trials. Traces align to contact onset.
rights_and_limitations: IEEE author copy. Bound applies only to the tested motions and controllers. The 2025 author data catalog assigns its third task, collision versus clamping, to this article.

authors: Tianyao Chen | Rafael Casas | Peter S. Lum
title: An Elbow Exoskeleton for Upper Limb Rehabilitation with Series Elastic Actuator and Cable-driven Differential
locator: Experimental evaluation, D. FE and SP Bandwidth and E. Impedance Measurement
evidence: Independent ATI Gamma connects bench to forearm ring. For a 0.01–15 Hz chirp, flexion/extension at 5.5 Nm crossed −3 dB at 3.94 ± 0.01 Hz. Supination/pronation at 5.6 Nm crossed at 3.68 ± 0.09 Hz. At higher flexion/extension amplitude the series-elastic mechanism would hit end stops near resonance.
rights_and_limitations: Public author manuscript. Mechanical end stops limit the test. That limit differs from electrical command clipping. ATI Mini40 at the handle serves another test.

authors: Marco Rossini | Sander De Bock | Vincent Ducastel | Gabriël Van De Velde | Kevin De Pauw | Tom Verstraten | Dirk Lefeber | Joost Geeroms | Carlos Rodriguez-Guerrero
title: Design and evaluation of AE4W: An active and flexible shaft-driven shoulder exoskeleton for workers
locator: Figs. 6–7, flexible-shaft/hypoid transmission testing and data availability statement
evidence: Bench setup uses independent 20 Nm and 2 Nm ETH Messtechnik DRBK transducers. For quasi-static transmission characterization a 0.05 Hz 0.1–0.6 Nm input sine was measured at the pinion. Testing addresses shaft/gear losses in torque transmission.
rights_and_limitations: Open Cambridge journal article. Raw files available by request to the corresponding author. Bench results do not establish synchronous pre/post limiter signals.

authors: Manuel Aiple | Wouter Gregoor | Andre Schiele
title: A Dynamic Robotic Actuator with Variable Physical Stiffness and Damping
source_version: arXiv v2 dated 5 August 2020, v1 June 2019 (early title: Design and Characterization of the Dynamic Robotic Actuator Dyrac). Author's TU Delft dissertation describes a submission to Mechanism and Machine Theory. No journal DOI confirmed.
locator: Figs. 10–14 and discussion of output-axis reference measurement
evidence: External loading with motor 1 fixed was measured by an ATI Gamma at the output axis, calibrated to ±10 Nm around z. Figs. 10–12 use the same observations. Centerline and line simplification were applied for display. The measured 90% stiffness adjustment took 50 ms for a small and 120 ms for a large step.
rights_and_limitations: Public arXiv manuscript. These data quantify stiffness/hysteresis under external loading, distinct from a measured closed-loop limit. DOI is the arXiv DOI.

authors: Aran Mohammad | Moritz Schappler | Tobias Ortmaier
title: Towards Human-Robot Collaboration with Parallel Robots by Kinetostatic Analysis, Impedance Control and Contact Detection
source_version: ICRA 2023, author manuscript arXiv:2308.09633. DOI confirmed by Leibniz University Hannover.
evidence: The bench uses two external force-torque sensors and a kinetostatic model to validate observer-based contact detection on a parallel robot. Comparisons project contact force to platform and actuated-joint coordinates.
rights_and_limitations: Public author manuscript. External projection, momentum observer and actual controlled joint torque have different physical meanings.
